result:
The smallest possible value is c = 2. I am recalling this from the known solution to this competition problem and have not re-derived the proof here.

The known result is that for every aquaesulian function f, the quantity f(r) + f(−r) takes at most two distinct values. There are also aquaesulian functions for which it takes exactly two, so the bound 2 cannot be lowered.

ANSWER: 2
